title: One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let f(x) = x^2 for x <= 1 and f(x) = 3 - x for x > 1. Find lim_{x -> 1^-} f(x), lim_{x -> 1^+} f(x), and determine whether lim_{x -> 1} f(x) exists.
finalAnswer: \lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = 1, \quad \lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = 2; \quad \lim_{x \to 1} f(x) \text{ does not exist (DNE)}

steps.title: Compute the Left-Hand Limit
steps.explanation: For x < 1, the rule f(x) = x^2 applies. Substitute x = 1.
steps.why: When evaluating from the left (x < 1), use the left branch.

steps.title: Compute the Right-Hand Limit
steps.explanation: For x > 1, the rule f(x) = 3 - x applies. Substitute x = 1.
steps.why: When evaluating from the right (x > 1), use the right branch.

steps.title: Compare One-Sided Limits
steps.explanation: Because the left-hand limit (1) does not equal the right-hand limit (2), the two-sided limit does not exist.
steps.why: Two-sided limit theorem asserts existence if and only if both one-sided limits are equal.
